question.text: What will be Bitcoin's hash rate on December 31, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as Bitcoin's "close" hash rate on December 31, 2026 according to [Coinmetrics.io](https://indexes.coinmetrics.io/cmbihash).
question.fine_print: No other source will be used.

research:
I've pulled the Coin Metrics page and the mempool.space difficulty data. Writing up now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-31: The CMBIHASH close was **1,091,535.86 PH/s**, the "most recent NY market close" on the page. Over 24 hours it was up 5.34%; for the year it is up 17.54%. The index uses a 48-hour lookback, so it swings a lot day to day. [Coin Metrics](https://indexes.coinmetrics.io/cmbihash)
- Daily closes from Oct 20 to Oct 31: 1,097,140; 967,859; 1,044,729; 1,076,176; 1,002,800; 1,083,164; 1,128,587 (the 7-day high, Oct 26); 1,069,188; 1,028,846; 1,003,033; 1,036,222; 1,091,536. [Coin Metrics](https://indexes.coinmetrics.io/cmbihash)
- Earlier closes: Oct 7, 976,408; Oct 9, 953,317; Oct 16, 971,353; Oct 19, 1,097,140. The 1-month range was 860,954 to 1,128,587. [Coin Metrics](https://indexes.coinmetrics.io/cmbihash)
- My own working from the page's percentages: the Dec 31, 2025 close was about 928,700 (from YTD +17.54%), and the Oct 31, 2025 close was about 1,077,700 (from 1Y +1.28%).
- Ranges shown on the page: 2-year high 1,203,394 (in Q4 2025), 1-year low 732,405 (in Q1 2026), Q3 2026 range 742,797 to 1,008,308.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The index sits near the middle of the 750k to 1,250k range.
- 2026-10-29: Difficulty rose 5.54% to 148.36T at block 973,728. That implies roughly 1,060 EH/s, or 1.06M PH/s. The previous adjustment, on Oct 16, was +5.92% to 140.58T. [mempool.space API](https://mempool.space/api/v1/mining/difficulty-adjustments/1y)
- 2026-11-01: The next retarget is projected around Nov 12 at about -0.46%. Average block time is about 593 seconds, which implies roughly 1.07M PH/s. [mempool.space](https://mempool.space/api/v1/difficulty-adjustment)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-31: BTC fell below $78K to $80K after the Fed held rates. Two dissenters favoured a hike, and a December hike is seen as possible. [TalkMarkets](https://talkmarkets.com/article/fed-holds-rates-at-375-4-as-two-dissents-back-a-hike-and-bitcoin-hovers-near-81k), [20minutos](https://www.20minutos.es/lainformacion/economia-y-finanzas/oro-cae-pese-inflacion-bitcoin-tampoco-responde-que-esta-fallando_7055552_0.html)

[oneminers](https://oneminers.com/blogs/news/bitcoin-difficulty-adjustment-october-29-2026-what-it-means-for-miners), [millionminer](https://millionminer.com/news/bitcoin-mining-update-october-2026)
- 2026-10-22: KuCoin, citing BlocksBridge, reported that the 7-day average hashrate passed 1 ZH/s for the first time since March 3, 2026. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/blog/bitcoin-hashrate-rebounds-in-2026-what-it-means-for-btc)
- Q3 2026: Hashrate Index put the Q3 average (30-day SMA) at about 940 EH/s, down 6.3% from Q2's 1,004. That was the second straight quarterly fall. Hashprice was near record lows in the low $30s. Analysts expected marginal capacity to go offline, and listed miners hold more than $70B in AI/HPC contracts. [Hashrate Index](https://hashrateindex.com/blog/global-hashrate-heatmap-update-q3-2026/)
- 2026-08-01: Difficulty was 14% below the year's high as miners pivoted to AI. [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/08/01/bitcoin-mining-difficulty-shrinks-14-from-this-year-s-high-as-plunging-revenues-force-operators-to-pivot)
- Pickaxe.io pages report 1,101 to 1,131 EH/s, but they look auto-generated and contradict themselves, so I gave them little weight. [Pickaxe](https://www.pickaxe.io/resources/news/bitcoin-hashrate-surges-past-1000-ehs-amid-difficulty-hikes)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- Last year's comparable window: the index went from about 1,077,700 (Oct 31, 2025) to about 928,700 (Dec 31, 2025), a drop of about 14%. Q4 2025 as a whole was -8.23%.
- Recent quarters on the index: Q1 2026 -8.68%, Q2 +3.20%, Q3 +11.23%. Q4 to date is +12.14%.
- Difficulty over the past 12 months ran from 125.8T to 152.3T, roughly 900 to 1,090 EH/s implied. Sharp drops have happened: -11.2% in February 2026 and -10.1% in mid-2026. So did sharp rises, such as +14.7% in February. [mempool.space](https://mempool.space/api/v1/mining/difficulty-adjustments/1y)
- Daily noise is large. Annualised volatility is about 107 to 118%, and over October the daily close moved within roughly ±10% of its trend. Any single day's close could land 5 to 10% away from the underlying hashrate.
- Over two months, 1-month ranges have spanned about 25%. The 3-month range was 773k to 1,129k.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on hashrate itself.
- Related Kalshi markets on BTC price at the end of 2026: the most likely bucket is $75K to $80K (18%), then $80K to $85K (16%) and $70K to $75K (13%). There is a 51% chance BTC hits $70K before $100K, and a 14% chance it crosses $100K before January 2027. Lower prices would put pressure on hashprice and could push marginal machines offline.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Difficulty retargets: about Nov 12 (currently projected at -0.46%), then roughly Nov 26, Dec 10 and Dec 24.
- 2026-12 FOMC: a possible rate hike, which could hit BTC price and therefore hashprice.
- Winter weather and grid curtailment in US mining regions. Hashrate fell in late December 2025 and again during the early-2026 winter storms, followed by difficulty cuts.
- More capacity moving from mining to AI/HPC, plus new-generation ASIC deliveries, which would push hashrate up.
- The resolution value is a single-day close with a 48-hour lookback, so block-time luck on Dec 30 and 31 will have a noticeable effect.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- Difficulty retargets fall roughly every 2 weeks: about Nov 12 (currently estimated -0.5%), then about Nov 25, about Dec 9 and about Dec 23. The Dec 31 value will reflect the 48 hours of block times before it.
- The December FOMC meeting carries a possible rate hike, which could weigh on BTC price and therefore hashprice.
- Winter conditions could matter:
  - Weather-driven curtailment or grid events in the US (Texas/ERCOT) and in Russia, where seasonal restrictions apply.
  - Cheaper hydro power ending in some regions.
- Miners may shift capacity to AI/HPC, and new ASIC deployments are coming online. I could not find specific scheduled figures for either.
- Random block-time luck on Dec 30 and 31 alone can move the close by ±5 to 10%.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 2 months. The question resolves on the CMBIHASH close for December 31, 2026, known around January 1, 2027.

**(b) Latest known value:** 1,091,535.86 PH/s on October 31, 2026, according to the Coin Metrics CMBIHASH close. October closes ranged from about 953k to 1,129k. The difficulty implies roughly 1.06M PH/s.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About 1.06 to 1.09M PH/s.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** Difficulty rose sharply twice in October, by 5.9% and 5.5%. However, the next retarget is projected to be flat (-0.46%), and hashprice is near record lows at about $34/PH/day. That points to a plateau, or modest growth to around 1.10 to 1.15M PH/s. Last year the index fell about 14% between Oct 31 and Dec 31 because of winter curtailment and a weak price, so the seasonal pattern argues for a softer number.

**(e) Historical variation:** Over two months, the underlying hashrate typically moves ±5 to 10%. One-month ranges have spanned about 25%. On top of that, the single-day close has noise of about ±5 to 10% because of the 48-hour block-luck lookback. Combined, I use a standard deviation of roughly 10%.

**(f) Experts and markets:** No market prices hashrate directly. Kalshi centres BTC at about $75 to 85K at year end and gives a 51% chance BTC hits $70K before $100K. That suggests continued pressure on hashprice and limits growth. Analysts expect marginal capacity to go offline and more miners to pivot to AI/HPC. New-generation ASIC deliveries partly offset this.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** BTC drops toward $60K after a December Fed hike. Combined with a severe US winter storm causing curtailment and an unlucky block run on December 30 and 31, the close could print around 800k.
- **High:** BTC rallies toward $100K and large new-generation ASIC fleets come online. With a lucky block streak, the close could reach about 1.3M.

I centre the median slightly below the current reading, at about 1,055k, to reflect the weak hashprice and the December seasonal pattern.
